title: VTA (apache/tvm-vta) -- the DefaultDe10Config accelerator
_note: Apache TVM's VTA, the Versatile Tensor Accelerator: the fetch / load /
compute / store pipeline, the GEMM core (TensorGemm, DotProduct, MAC, the
adder tree), the tensor ALU, the VME and VCR bus / register interfaces, the
tensor load / store paths and their queues -- 66 rows.
VTA is Chisel, but it pins **chisel3 3.5.0**, which predates the
org.chipsalliance Chisel 6 line that rocket-chip / BOOM / Gemmini use, so it
cannot be compiled against the rocket-chip checkout's modules the way
boom_setup.sh and gemmini_setup.sh do.  It does not need to be: VTA ships a
`make verilog` target, and Chisel 3.5 emits SystemVerilog through the Scala
FIRRTL compiler with no firtool involved.  test/ext_ip/vta_setup.sh installs
sbt (one launcher tarball, as the other setups install mill / firtool /
bender) and runs that target; the artifacts resolve from Maven Central and
the build works on the JDK 17 already present.
The emitted file is ONE SystemVerilog file holding every module
(build/chisel/VTA.DefaultDe10Config.sv, 23.6k lines, 67 modules), not one
file per module as firtool produces -- so every row's closure is that whole
file, which at 1.3 MB costs nothing.
Only `IntelShell` is excluded: it is the DE10 board wrapper and the sole
vendor-specific module in the file; everything else is vendor-neutral VTA
RTL.  DefaultPynqConfig (Xilinx) and DefaultF1Config are the other two
configurations the repository defines -- one VTA_CONFIG away if the shell
ever matters.
First local sweep 2026-10-28 (66 rows): 47 / 66 proven, **66 / 66
elaborate, 66 / 66 co-sim PASS, 66 rows with 0 undriven, 0 divergences, 0
`differs`, 0 read-fails and not one row without a read_slang reference**.
1.0 h of row time.
Every one of the 19 unproven rows is a SAT-BUDGET row (15 over the memory
cap, 4 timeout) and every one of them co-simulates clean: Core, Compute,
Load, Store, LoadUopTop, DotProduct and the other wide datapath blocks.  So
the family has no open reader lead at all -- the cleanest of the campaign,
cleaner even than gemmini (which had the same zero divergences but 1
elab-fail).
